newsitem.title: USA: Stocks tumble under pressure from rising interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Stocks tumble under pressure from rising interest rates.

text.p: Stocks tumbled Friday as investors sold off under the mounting pressure of surging interest rates propelled by fresh inflation worries.
The Dow Jones industrial average slid 156.78 points to 8,031.22. It was the ninth-largest point decline ever for the blue-chip average.
In the broader market, decliners beat advancers 2,456 to 526 on heavy volume of 561 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange. For the week, the Dow fell 162.82 points.
As on Thursday, when the Dow fell 71 points, stocks got hurt Friday by weakness in the bond market, where the yield on the 30-year Treasury jumped to 6.64 percent from 6.53 percent.

"The two props to valuation levels in this market have been interest rates, which have been trending lower, and earnings, which have been surprisingly good," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"This month, at least so far, we have had the bond market reversing course and nothing sufficiently positive to hold the market up," he said.
The rapid turnaround in interest rates has come amid a sudden flurry of signs that economic growth may have started to accelerate after a tame second quarter.
